title: Enzyme inhibition assays and human interaction references
scope: Measured in-vitro inhibitor constants, explicitly derived clearance fractions, and separate human study observations. No clinical combination prediction.

inhibitionAssays.system: Pooled human liver microsomes; dextromethorphan O-demethylation; competitive inhibition fit

components.label: Racemic bupropion parent
components.bindingEvidence: Approximation to measured near-unity microsomal unbound fractions; paper reports negligible binding correction (Supplemental Table 2).
components.fractionEvidence: Racemic parent assay; no metabolite allocation.

assumptions: Free plasma is a proxy for hepatic inhibitor concentration; no hepatic accumulation is simulated.
The catalog plasma free fraction is retained; this is not a reproduction of the study's plasma-binding experiment.
The hydroxy-, threo-, and erythrohydrobupropion metabolites are omitted. Parent-only inhibition can severely underrepresent the clinical interaction.

inhibitionAssays.system: Pooled human liver microsomes from six donors; dextromethorphan O-demethylation; reversible inhibition
inhibitionAssays.evidenceType: in-vitro measurement plus estimated enantiomer mixture

components.label: R-fluoxetine parent
components.bindingEvidence: Table 2 footnote m explicitly identifies total Ki and incubation fraction unbound; unbound Ki is their product, applied once.
components.fractionEvidence: Estimated equal share of the modeled unbound racemic parent pool; stereoselective disposition is not modeled.

components.label: S-fluoxetine parent
components.bindingEvidence: Table 2 footnote m explicitly identifies total Ki and incubation fraction unbound; unbound Ki is their product, applied once.
components.fractionEvidence: Estimated equal share of the modeled unbound racemic parent pool; stereoselective disposition is not modeled.

assumptions: Free plasma substitutes for unbound hepatic exposure; the catalog parent free fraction is retained.
The 50:50 unbound R:S split is assumed, not a measured steady-state enantiomer ratio.
Norfluoxetine, time-dependent enzyme effects, induction, and nonlinear self-inhibition are not dynamically modeled.

clearanceModels.evidenceType: derived estimate, not measured fraction metabolized
assumptions: Treat quinidine blockade of CYP2D6 as complete and selective and assume unchanged bioavailability and other clearance routes.
Incomplete blockade would imply a higher true fraction; this derived fraction is not a measured individual parameter.
Transfer an oral parent-drug AUC ratio to the simulation's plasma clearance; active dehydro-aripiprazole is omitted.

clearanceModels.evidenceType: derived estimate, not measured fraction metabolized
assumptions: Use the normal-metabolizer subgroup, not the pooled all-genotype ratio, and treat paroxetine inhibition as complete and selective.
Assume unchanged oral bioavailability and residual clearance when transferring the AUC ratio to plasma elimination.
The transformed study interval covers sampling uncertainty only; it does not cover the complete-blockade assumption or cross-inhibitor transfer.

clinicalReferences.title: Aripiprazole + quinidine: human reference
clinicalReferences.result: Parent AUC increased 112%; active-metabolite AUC decreased 35%.
clinicalReferences.regimen: Study protocol: aripiprazole 10 mg once with quinidine 166 mg/day for 13 days.
clinicalReferences.population: Human interaction study summarized in ABILIFY prescribing information.
clinicalReferences.applicability: Quinidine is a reference inhibitor, not an added exposure. Its observed AUC ratio informs a derived clearance fraction, not a predicted AUC for the current mixture.

clinicalReferences.title: LSD + paroxetine: human reference
clinicalReferences.endpoint: LSD plasma AUC in CYP2D6 normal metabolizers
clinicalReferences.result: Normal-metabolizer subgroup AUC ratio 1.76 (90% CI 1.44–2.14); whole-cohort ratio was approximately 1.5.
clinicalReferences.regimen: Study protocol: LSD 100 µg once after paroxetine 10 mg/day for 7 days then 20 mg/day for 35 days, versus placebo pretreatment.
clinicalReferences.population: Randomized crossover trial in 23 healthy adults; CYP2D6 normal-metabolizer subgroup n = 11.
clinicalReferences.applicability: Paroxetine is a reference inhibitor, not an added exposure. Higher AUC does not imply proportionately stronger subjective effects or apply as a multiplier to another SSRI.

clinicalReferences.title: Bupropion + desipramine: human reference
clinicalReferences.result: Approximately fivefold AUC and twofold peak concentration; interaction persisted after bupropion was stopped.
clinicalReferences.regimen: Study protocol: repeated bupropion 150 mg twice daily, then desipramine 50 mg once.
clinicalReferences.population: 15 male CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers, ages 19–35, summarized in prescribing information.
clinicalReferences.applicability: Desipramine is not an added exposure. This includes metabolite effects; a small parent-only calculated effect must not be read as a small clinical interaction.

clinicalReferences.title: Fluoxetine + diazepam: observed interaction
clinicalReferences.result: Diazepam AUC and half-life increased and clearance decreased; no significant change in the measured psychomotor response.
clinicalReferences.regimen: Study protocol: diazepam 10 mg once, alone, after fluoxetine 60 mg once, and after eight daily fluoxetine administrations.
clinicalReferences.population: Six healthy participants; within-subject pharmacokinetic study.
clinicalReferences.applicability: Qualitative study direction is displayed only. No numeric multiplier is inferred from the abstract or applied to this mixture; active-metabolite compensation and CYP2C19/CYP3A4 mechanisms are omitted.

clinicalReferences.title: Escitalopram + desipramine: human reference
clinicalReferences.result: Desipramine AUC increased 100% and peak concentration increased 40%.
clinicalReferences.regimen: Study protocol: escitalopram 20 mg/day for 21 days with desipramine 50 mg once.
clinicalReferences.population: Human interaction study summarized in escitalopram prescribing information.
clinicalReferences.applicability: The catalog omits this weak-inhibition concentration curve. Desipramine is a reference probe, not an added exposure; its twofold AUC is not transferred to another substrate.

limitations: These calculations cover selected reversible parent-drug CYP2D6 effects only. Metabolites, liver accumulation, enzyme turnover, induction and genotype-specific kinetics are not modeled.
Observed study AUC ratios are evidence cards; they are never concentration-independent multipliers of another drug's time course.
Self-inhibition is omitted because the supplied terminal half-lives already reflect clinical parent-drug disposition and no calibrated nonlinear self-inhibition model is available.
A factor of one for an unsupported pathway means no change was calculated, not evidence of no interaction.
Binding competition is separate from enzyme competition. Functional-response pooling, baseline transmitter levels, cross-assay transfer and clinical consequences remain estimated.
